Convert an object to a hawkes

Source: R/hawkes_object.R
as_hawkes.Rd

Convert an object to a hawkes

Usage

as_hawkes(
  data,
  time_window,
  spatial_region,
  spatial_family,
  temporal_family,
  covariate_columns = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Data frame with columns x, y, and t, or an sf object with event geometry and a t column.

time_window

Numeric vector of length two specifying the observation window.

spatial_region

sf object defining the spatial domain.

spatial_family

Spatial triggering kernel or list of custom kernel helpers.

temporal_family

Temporal triggering kernel or list of custom kernel helpers.

covariate_columns

Optional character vector naming background covariates.

Value

A hawkes object.

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  x = runif(100, 0, 10),
  y = runif(100, 0, 10),
  t = runif(100, 0, 50)
)

# Convert to hawkes object
spatial_region <- create_rectangular_sf(0, 10, 0, 10)
hawkes_df <- as_hawkes(
  df,
  c(0, 50),
  spatial_region,
  spatial_family = "Gaussian",
  temporal_family = "Exponential"
)
print(hawkes_df)
